main_text.l: unam tantum perpessus fuerit: sed persisten-
dum est vsque ad finem, donec cursum con-
summauerimus. Sit igitur hæc assidua pio-
rum meditatio, vbi pluribus ærumnis per-
functi fuerint, ad nouas ferendas se parare,
nec vnquam fatigentur, etiamsi quotidiana fit-
crux illorum. Et hoc est, quod Dominus Ie-
sus dixit, Matth. 10. Qui perseuerauerit vsq;
in finem, hic saluus erit. Graue quidem, quo-
tidie premi cruce: graue quoque habere vxo-
rem rixosam, quæ instar perfluentis stillici-
dij est: sed si cogites etiam Christū Dominū
tulisse crucem suam, & quotidie multa ferre
à sponsa sua: item si vitæ sequentis æternita-
tem, & istius breuitatem & fugacitatem con-
sideres, leue erit quod in se graue putatur:
idque per Iesum Christum Dominum no-
strum, cui sit gloria & imperium in omne
ævum, Amen.
CONCIO XLIIII
Matth. 19.

page.notes: The woodcut initial at the start of the last paragraph shows a letter that I cannot read with certainty, so it is not transcribed. The hyphen-like mark in "fit-crux" is unclear and may be a stop; I have written it with a hyphen as printed. The signature at the foot ("S s") is partly worn and may read differently. The running head "NVPTIALES" has a decorative first letter that is uncertain. The page number "281" is partly worn.
